observations: Photo 0: Front view of a black DSLR body with 'Canon' and 'EOS 5D' markings, body cap on (no lens attached), screen in background is a TV not the camera's screen.
Photo 1: Rear view of the same body, screen appears off/black, Canon logo visible on bottom, no battery, charger, or trigger visible.
Photo 2: Front view resting on a sofa, 'Canon' logo and 'MarkIII' text visible on bottom right of body, body cap still on, small LCD top display shows some digits.
No batteries, charger, or Godox trigger are visible in any of the three photos.
No lens is shown in any photo; all shots show a body cap, so lens condition (fungus/scratch) cannot be seen.
Camera's own rear screen is never shown powered on with an image, so screen/function cannot be judged.
No shutter-count readout (e.g., from EOS Utility or a shutter-count app) is shown in any photo.

claims.evidence: No shutter-count screenshot or menu display shown in any photo.

claims.claim: No fungus or scratch on the lens
claims.evidence: No lens is shown in any photo; body cap is on in all three shots.
No batteries visible in any photo.
No charger visible in any photo.
No trigger visible in any photo.

claims.evidence: No internal or serial-plate evidence shown; repair history cannot be seen from exterior photos.

risks.risk: Shutter count could be far higher than claimed, affecting mechanical wear and price.
risks.proof: A photo or screenshot of the shutter count from the camera's menu or software (e.g., EOS Info, ShutterCount app).
risks.if_unproven: priced as high-use/unknown shutter count, i.e. body-only worst case

risks.risk: Rear LCD screen may be cracked, dead, or malfunctioning; it is shown off/black in photo 1.
risks.proof: A photo or video of the screen powered on displaying a live image or menu.

risks.risk: No lens is included or shown, despite a claim about lens condition, creating ambiguity about what is actually being sold.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the lens (if any) mounted on the body, or confirmation that this is body-only.
risks.if_unproven: priced as body only, no lens

risks.risk: Claimed accessories (2 batteries, charger, Godox trigger) are not visible in any photo.
risks.proof: A single photo showing the camera body together with both batteries, the charger, and the Godox trigger.
risks.if_unproven: priced as body only, accessories not confirmed

risks.risk: Sensor/mount condition (corrosion, dust, fungus inside mount) cannot be assessed with body cap on.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the lens mount and sensor with the cap removed.
risks.if_unproven: priced as condition unknown, treated as cosmetic-only verified

risks.risk: No proof of functional shutter actuation (test shot or video of mirror/shutter firing).
risks.proof: A short video of the shutter firing or a sample photo taken with the camera, with EXIF visible.

proof_requests: Photo/screenshot of the shutter count from the camera menu or a shutter-count checking tool.
Video or photo of the rear screen powered on showing a live view or menu.
Photo of the camera together with both batteries, the charger, and the Godox trigger.
Photo of the lens mount and sensor with the body cap removed.
Short video of the shutter firing or a sample test photo with EXIF data.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a Canon EOS 5D Mark III body from photos 0 and 2, but no lens, batteries, charger, or trigger are actually visible, and shutter count, screen function, and lens condition are all unverifiable, so it must be priced at the worst case as a body-only unit of unconfirmed functional condition, matching the one directly comparable listing for the same model sold as body alone.
